newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics gives U.S. workers holiday.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics gives U.S. workers holiday.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc. said its roughly 7,000 U.S. employees will start the company's next fiscal year on holiday.

The company, which makes powerful compute-intensive computers used in applications ranging from special effects for film productions to industrial design, has been struggling to return its business to steady growth after a series of earnings shortfalls.
A spokesman said the company would give its U.S. employees holiday on the first and second, in addition to the third of July, which is a national holiday in observance of Independence Day, July 4.

"The biggest reason for this is cost savings and it's also a chance as we move into the new fiscal year for employees to take a break and get ready for fiscal 1998," the spokesman said. "It's not unusual for Silicon Valley companies to do this at the new (business) year."

"It's no secret that we've been going through this difficult product transition," he added, referring to the company's effort to upgrade its entire product line since last autumn, "As of the end of March we've been able to ship our entire product line without constraints that we saw over the previous several quarters."
The company could not say whether the savings would be material to its earnings in the first quarter of its fiscal 1998, which begins on July 1.
Silicon Graphics offered similar holidays to employees in 1991 and 1993, the company said.
